questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Pressure in a reservoir of water is same at all points at the same level of water.

Statement II: The pressure applied to enclosed water is transmitted in all directions equally.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are false
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is true but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is false
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is false but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is true
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Pressure in a static fluid will be same at each point on same horizontal level.

P=P0+ρgh

where P0 is atmospheric pressure.

Pascal's law states that pressure applied to enclosed water is transmitted equally in all directions. Hence, both the statements are true and this is the right option.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The contact angle between a solid and a liquid is a property of the material of the solid and liquid as well.
Statement II : The rise of a liquid in a capillary tube does not depend on the inner radius of the tube.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct as we know contact angle depends on cohesine and adhesive forces.
Statement II is incorrect because height of liquid is given by $h==\frac{2 T \cos \theta_C}{\rho g r}$ where $r$ is radius of Tube (assuming length of capillary is sufficient).

questions.q: Consider a completely full cylindrical water tank of height 1.6 m and cross-sectional area $0.5 \mathrm{~m}^2$. It has a small hole in its side at a height 90 cm from the bottom. Assume, the cross-sectional area of the hole to be negligibly small as compared to that of the water tank. If a load 50 kg is applied at the top surface of the water in the tank then the velocity of the water coming out at the instant when the hole is opened is : $\left(\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Apply Bernouli equation between points $1 \& 2$
$\begin{aligned}
& P_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2+\rho g h=P_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2+0 \\ & P_0+\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{~A}}+\rho g \frac{70}{100}=P_0+\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2 \\ & \frac{5000}{0.5}+10^3 \times 10 \frac{70}{100}=\frac{1}{2} \times 10^3 v_2^2
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
& 10^3+10^3 \times 7=\frac{10^3}{2} \mathrm{v}_2^2 \\ & \mathrm{v}_2^2=16 \\ & \mathrm{v}_2=4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$
As the tank area is large $\mathrm{v}_1$ is negligible compared to $\mathrm{v}_2$

questions.q: A small ball of mass $m$ and density $\rho$ is dropped in a viscous liquid of density $\rho_0$. After sometime, the ball falls with constant velocity. The viscous force on the ball is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{ma}\mathrm{a}=0$ for constant velocity
$\begin{aligned}
& m g-F_B=F_v \\
& F_v=m g-v \rho_0 g=m g-\frac{m}{\rho} \rho_0 g=m g\left(1-\frac{\rho_0}{\rho}\right)
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An air bubble of radius 0.1 cm lies at a depth of 20 cm below the free surface of a liquid of density $1000 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$. If the pressure inside the bubble is $2100 \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}^2$ greater than the atmospheric pressure, then the surface tension of the liquid in SI unit is (use $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & P_1=P_0+\rho g h=P_0+1000 \times 10 \times \frac{20}{100} \\ & \Rightarrow P_1=P_0+2000 \end{aligned}$ So, $P_2-P_1=\frac{2 S}{R}=\left(\frac{2 S}{1 \times 10^{-3}}\right)\Rightarrow P_2=P_0+2100$ (given) $\begin{aligned} & \text { So, } P_0+2100-P_0-2000=2 S \times 10^3 \\ & \Rightarrow 100=2 S \times 10^3 \\ & \Rightarrow s=\left(\frac{1}{20}\right)=0.05 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A liquid of density $\rho$ is coming out of a hose pipe of radius a with horizontal speed $v$ and hits a mesh. $50 \%$ of the liquid passes through the mesh unaffected. $25 \%$ looses all of its momentum and $25 \%$ comes back with the same speed. The resultant pressure on the mesh will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Mass per unit time of the liquid = \rhoav Momentum per second carried by liquid $=\rho a v \times v$

Net force due to bounced back liquid, $\mathrm{F}_{1}=2 \times\left[\frac{1}{4} \rho \mathrm{av}^{2}\right]$

Net force due to stopped liquid, $\mathrm{F}_{2}=\frac{1}{4}$ pav $^{2}$ Total force,

$\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{F}_{1}+\mathrm{F}_{2}=\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{av}^{2}+\frac{1}{4} \mathrm{pav}^{2}=\frac{3}{4} \mathrm{pav}^{2}$

Net pressure $=\frac{3}{4} \rho v^{2}$

questions.q: An air bubble of volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> rises from the bottom of a lake <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> deep to the surface at a temperature of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>12</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The atmospheric pressure is  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi><mo>,</mo></math> the density of water is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo><mo> </mo></math>There is no difference of the temperature of water at the depth of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and on the surface. The volume of air bubble when it reaches the surface will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The pressure at the bottom of the lake can be calculated as follows:

Pbottom= P0 + ρgh=105+1000 × 10 × 40 Pa=5×105 Pa 

As the temperature of water remains constant, it can be written that

PbottomVbottom=PtopVtop   ...(1)

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface.

5×105×1=1×105×Vtop⇒Vtop=5×105×11×105 cm3= 5 cm3

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: Statement I : When speed of liquid is zero everywhere, pressure difference at any two points depends on equation $P_1-P_2=\rho g\left(h_2-h_1\right)$. Statement II : In ventury tube shown $2 \mathrm{gh}=v_1^2-v_2^2$
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's equation $\mathrm{P}_1+\rho \mathrm{gh}_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_1^2=\mathrm{P}_2+\rho \mathrm{gh}_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_2^2\left[h_1 \& h_2\right.$ are height of point from any reference level] Given $\mathrm{V}_1=\mathrm{V}_2=0$ (for statement-1) $\therefore \mathrm{P}_1-\mathrm{P}_2=\mathrm{g}\left(\mathrm{h}_2-\mathrm{h}_2\right)$
For statement-2 $\mathrm{P}_1+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_1^2=\mathrm{P}_2+\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{v}_2^2\begin{aligned} & P_1-P_2=\rho g h \\ & P_1-P_2=\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2-\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2 \\ & \rho g h=\frac{1}{2} \rho v_2^2-\frac{1}{2} \rho v_1^2 \\ & 2 g h=v_2^2-v_1^2 \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A glass tumbler having inner depth of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>17</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is kept on a table. A student starts pouring water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math> into it while looking at the surface of water from the above. When he feels that the tumbler is half filled, he stops pouring water. Up to what height, the tumbler is actually filled ?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Height of water observed by observer
=Hμw=H(4/3)=3H4

Height of air observed by observer =17.5-H

According to question, both height observed by observer is same.
3H4=17.5-H

⇒  H=10 cm

questions.q: In an experiment to verify Stokes law, a small spherical ball of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> and density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ρ</mi></math> falls under gravity through a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> in air before entering a tank of water. If the terminal velocity of the ball inside water is same as its velocity just before entering the water surface, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math> is proportional to: (ignore viscosity of air)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The velocity of ball just before striking the surface of water is given by using kinematical equation of motion under the gravity

v2=u2-2gy

⇒v2=-2g(-h)

⇒v=2gh  ...(1) 

Now, the terminal velocity of spherical ball inside the water tank is given by,

vT=29r2(ρ-σ)gη  ...(2)

After falling through h the velocity of ball should be equal to its terminal velocity.

From equation (1) and (2) we get,

⇒2gh=29r2(ρ-σ)gη

Squaring the above equation, we get

⇒h=281r4g(ρ-σ)2η2

⇒h∝r4

questions.q:
The figure shows a liquid of given density flowing steadily in horizontal tube of varying cross-section. Cross-sectional areas at A is 1.5 cm2, and B is 25 mm2, if the speed of liquid at B is 60 cm s-1 then (PA–PB) is

(Given PA and PB are liquid pressures at A and B points.

Density ρ=1000 kg m-3

A and B are on the axis of tube)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using Bernoulli's theorem,

PA+12ρVA2=PB+12ρVB2   ...(i)

Using equation of continuity,

AAVA=ABVB

So, 1.5×10-4×VA=25×10-6×VB

VA=25×10-61.5×10-4×0.6

=110 m s-1

Substituting in equation (i)

⇒PA-PB=100020.62-0.12=10002×0.7×0.5

=175 Pa

questions.q: A submarine experiences a pressure of <math><mn>5.05</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math> at a depth of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> in a sea. When it goes further to a depth of <math><mi> </mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> , it experiences a pressure of <math><mi> </mi><mn>8.08</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math> . Then <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> is approximately (density of water <math><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></math> and acceleration due to gravity <math><mi> </mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> ):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The pressure at a depth d is p=p0+ρgd, here p0 is the atmospheric pressure.
∴p1=p0+ρgd1
and p2=p0+ρgd2
The difference in pressure is p2-p1=ρgd2-d1

Putting the values in the above equation
8.08×106-5.05×106=103×10d2-d1
d2-d1=3.03×106104
=303 m

(The coefficient of viscosity of water is $9.8 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{~s} / \mathrm{m}^2$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}& \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{T}}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~g}}{9} \frac{\mathrm{R}^2\left[\rho_{\mathrm{B}}-\rho_{\mathrm{L}}\right]}{\eta} \\& \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{T}}=\frac{2}{9} \times \frac{10 \times\left(10^{-4}\right)^2}{9.8 \times 10^{-6}}\left[10^5-10^3\right] \\& \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{T}}=224.5\end{aligned}$
when ball fall from height (h)

questions.q: A hydraulic press can lift <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> when a mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is placed on the smaller piston. questions.q:
A vessel with square cross-section and height of 6 m is vertically partitioned. A small window of $100 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ with hinged door is fitted at a depth of 3 m in the partition wall. One part of the vessel is filled completely with water and the other side is filled with the liquid having density $1.5 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$. What force one needs to apply on the hinged door so that it does not get opened ?
(Acceleration due to gravity $=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
in equilibrium
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{F}_{\text {ext }}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{w}}=\mathrm{F}_{\ell} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{F}_{\text {ext }}=\mathrm{F}_{\ell}-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{w}} \\ & =\left(\mathrm{P}_0+\rho_{\ell} \mathrm{gh}\right) \mathrm{A}-\left(\mathrm{P}_0+\rho_{\mathrm{w}} \mathrm{gh}\right) \mathrm{A} \\ & =\left(\rho_{\ell}-\rho_{\mathrm{w}}\right) \mathrm{ghA} \\ & =(1500-1000) \times 10 \times 3 \times\left(100 \times 10^{-4}\right) \\ & =150 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Glycerin of density 1.25×103 kg m–3 is flowing through the conical section of pipe. The area of cross-section of the pipe at its ends are 10 cm2 and 5 cm2 and pressure drop across its length is 3 N m–2. The rate of flow of glycerine through the pipe is x×10–5 m3 s–1. The value of x is _____.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
It is given that

A1=10 cm2; A2=5 cm2

∆P=3 N m-2

By continuity equation,

A1v1=A2v2⇒v1=A2v2A1   ...(i)

By Bernoulli's equation,

12ρv22-12ρv12=∆P   ...(ii)

Using equation (i) in (ii)

∆P=ρ2(v22-A2v2A12)⇒∆P=ρv2221-A2A12⇒3=1.25×103×v2221-14⇒v22=6×41.25×103×3⇒v2=8×10-2 m s-1

So, the discharge rate is,

A2v2=x×10-5⇒x=5×10-4×8×10-210-5=4

questions.q:
The area of cross-section of a large tank is 0.5 m2. It has a narrow opening near the bottom having area of cross-section 1 cm2. A load of 25 kg is applied on the water at the top in the tank. Neglecting the speed of water in the tank, the velocity of the water, coming out of the opening at the time when the height of water level in the tank is 40 cm above the bottom, will be _____ cm s-1.

[Take g=10 m s-2 ]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Pressure at point 1 is P1=P0, Pressure at point 2 is P2=P0+mgA

Applying Bernoulli's equation at top and bottom

P1+12ρv12+ρgh1=P2+12ρv22+ρgh2⇒P0+12ρv2+0=P0+mgA+0+ρgh

⇒2505+103×10×0.4=12×103×v2

v=3 m s-1=300 cm s-1

questions.q: A liquid column of height $0.04 \mathrm{~cm}$ balances excess pressure of a soap bubble of certain radius. If density of liquid is $8 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$ and surface tension of soap solution is $0.28 \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$, then diameter of the soap bubble is _____ $\mathrm{cm}$. (if $g=10 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \rho \mathrm{gh}=\frac{4 \mathrm{~S}}{\mathrm{R}} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}=\frac{4 \times 0.28}{8 \times 10^3 \times 10 \times 4 \times 10^{-4}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{0.28}{8} \mathrm{~m}=\frac{28}{8} \mathrm{~cm} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}=3.5 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$
Diameter $=7 \mathrm{~cm}$
